title: Number of Closed Islands
prompt: You are given an `m x n` binary matrix `grid` where `0` represents land and `1` represents water. An island is a maximal 4-directionally connected group of `0`s. A closed island is an island that is totally enclosed by water (`1`s) — it does not touch the border of the grid on any side. Return the number of closed islands.

examples.explanation: There are two islands of 0s that are completely surrounded by 1s and don't touch the grid border.
Every island of land touches the border, so none are closed.

hints: An island touching the border can never be closed, no matter its shape — handle border-connected land first.
Flood-fill (DFS/BFS) from every land cell on the border and eliminate (flip to water) everything connected to it, so only interior islands remain.
After removing all border-connected land, count the remaining islands exactly like the classic number-of-islands problem — every one left is guaranteed closed.

solution.approach: First flood-fill from every land cell that sits on the grid's border, flipping all land connected to the border to water — none of that land can ever belong to a closed island. Once border-touching land is eliminated, any remaining land cell must belong to an island fully enclosed by water, so a standard flood-fill count over what's left directly gives the number of closed islands.
